display.title: Episode 308: Shabbos Chazak and Asarah B'Teves
display.summary_short: Finishing Sefer Bereishis on Shabbos Chazak, two young guests from Ann Arbor say the Shema, the meaning of the fast of Asarah B'Teves, and a family's letter from the mailbox.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in Teves 5748, the week of Parshas Vayechi and Asarah B'Teves. Uncle Yossi explains that this Shabbos we finish Sefer Bereishis and call out 'Chazak, chazak, v'nischazek', asking Hashem for strength to keep learning, just as we do on Simchas Torah, and urges children to be in shul to join in. After the Hakochainik march, a brother and sister visiting from Ann Arbor, Michigan, lead the Shema. Then comes the month of Teves: as Shlomo HaMelech said, there is a time for everything, even a time to be sad so that we improve. On the tenth of Teves the armies of Nevuchadnetzar besieged Yerushalayim, which led to the breach of the walls on Shiva Asar B'Tammuz and the destruction of the Beis HaMikdash on Tisha B'Av. As long as we learn Torah and keep mitzvos, the Guardian of Israel protects us, and soon Moshiach will turn these fast days into holidays. This Thursday we fast, give tzedakah and cry 'Ad mosai!'. The mailbox brings a mother's letter about her children and their drawings of Tzivos Hashem rooms, and the show ends with Shabbos candle time.
display.lesson: Remembering sad days in our history helps us improve; Torah and mitzvos protect us, and Moshiach will turn the fasts into holidays.

date.note: Consistent with the audio: Parshas Vayechi this Shabbos, 'this Thursday is Asarah B'Teves' (31 Dec 1987), Shabbos candles Friday January 1st at 4:21.

advisories.note: Explains the siege of Yerushalayim, hunger in the city and the destruction of the Beis HaMikdash, told gently.

Family's street address read in the mailbox.

'The Guardian of Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps.'
